holidays.name: National Grammar Day
holidays.description: A day for word nerds to celebrate proper punctuation, dangling modifiers, and the Oxford comma. It is the only holiday that doubles as a command: March forth on March 4th!
holidays.origin: Founded in 2008 by Martha Brockenbrough, who also founded the Society for the Promotion of Good Grammar. The date was chosen because March 4 sounds like a command to 'march forth' and speak well.
holidays.funFact: Brockenbrough's society has been known to give out 'Grammar Hero' recognition, and the day has inspired countless social media debates about the Oxford comma.

holidays.name: National Pound Cake Day
holidays.description: A buttery tribute to the dense, golden dessert that is sliced thick and served with berries, whipped cream, or a quiet sense of triumph.
holidays.origin: A food holiday of unofficial origin, celebrating a cake whose name comes from its original recipe: one pound each of butter, sugar, eggs, and flour. The recipe dates back to 18th-century Europe.
holidays.funFact: The original recipe was so simple that it was easy to remember for bakers who couldn't read, and it made a gigantic cake that fed a crowd.

holidays.name: Hug a GI Day
holidays.description: A day to thank members of the military by giving them a hug, a handshake, or a heartfelt thank you, while also reminding everyone that service members are people, too.
holidays.origin: An informal observance in the United States created to encourage appreciation for service members. It is celebrated by individuals and community groups rather than any official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: The term 'GI' originally stood for 'galvanized iron,' used to describe military trash cans, before it became shorthand for 'government issue' and then for soldiers themselves.

holidays.name: World Day of Engineering for Sustainable Development
holidays.description: A global celebration of engineers who solve the world's biggest problems, from clean water to green energy, often while being told 'it's just a small bridge.'
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2019 to highlight the role of engineering in achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals. It is observed annually on March 4.
holidays.funFact: UNESCO notes that engineering is behind almost every technology we use, yet fewer than one in three engineering students worldwide are women, which the day aims to change.

holidays.name: Courageous Conversations Global Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to having the tough chats everyone avoids, whether about feelings, boundaries, or who really ate the last slice of pound cake.
holidays.origin: Started as an awareness observance encouraging people to speak honestly and respectfully about difficult topics like race, mental health, and workplace issues, and it spread through social media and community organizations.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists say most people overestimate how bad a hard conversation will go, so the day is basically a nudge to rip off the conversational Band-Aid.
